chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Would something occur today that was not in the knowledge of God yesterday?' He said: 'No. Whoever says this, may God disgrace him.'

I said: 'What is your view of what has occurred and what will continue to occur until the Day of Resurrection — is it not within the knowledge of God?' He said: 'Yes indeed, (even) before He created the creatures.'

key_terms.بَلَى: Yes indeed — a strong affirmative particle used to confirm a negatively-phrased question
key_terms.عِلْمِ اللَّهِ: Knowledge of God — His omniscience, pre-eternal and all-encompassing, admitting no increase or change
key_terms.فَأَخْزَاهُ اللَّهُ: May God disgrace him — an imprecatory formula signalling the gravity of denying divine omniscience
key_terms.كَائِنٌ: Coming to be/occurring — active participle (ism fa'il) denoting future events yet to materialise

ai.seo_question: Does Shia theology teach that God's knowledge encompasses all past and future events, even before the creation of the universe?
ai.summary: Mansur ibn Hazim questions Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about whether any event can fall outside God's pre-eternal knowledge. The Imam emphatically rejects this, invoking divine disgrace upon those who assert otherwise, and affirms that God's knowledge encompassed all past and future events even before the creation of the universe. This hadith appears in the chapter on Bada' to clarify that the doctrine does not imply any temporal acquisition of knowledge by God.
